window.status: 12 credentials, 2 look stale, every secret hidden
notes: Every row shows its secret as dots and never as text; the dots are drawn from the secret's absence, not from reading it, so a row that shows dots holds nothing to leak.
Each row state is shown with an icon and a word: Generic credential, Domain password, Looks stale, Session only. Colour alone never carries the state.

Refresh is the accent button: it lists the credentials again and the rows update from that re-read. Reveal is beside it and acts on the one selected row; with no row or several rows selected it is disabled with a tooltip saying why.

Reveal when the tool is not elevated is refused by name: the message says Reveal needs administrator rights, nothing is read, and the Activity section records the refusal. A domain password is refused with the reason that Windows lets no program read it back.
A revealed secret is shown for a short time in that one row, then hidden again; it is never copied to the clipboard or to a log, and each reveal writes one Activity line naming the target.
The status bar states the counts in words, for example "12 credentials, 2 look stale, every secret hidden".
There is no Reveal all and no export, in the window or anywhere else; the plan proves this by a search of the source.
window.cut: There is no earlier window to cut from: the tool is new. It has no menus, no splash, no animations and no donate strip, and it builds none of them; the framework's Settings and About pages replace what a menu would hold. Nothing in the window can show every secret at once, and that absence is the design, recorded in the plan.

readme.lead: Credential Viewer shows which sign-ins Windows has saved for you, with every secret kept hidden.
what: Windows keeps saved sign-ins in Credential Manager: website and share passwords, remembered network logins and the like. The built-in view is hard to read and tells you nothing about which saved sign-in is wrong. Credential Viewer lists every stored credential by its target, its type and its user name, with the time it was last changed and its secret shown only as dots.

It also points at credentials that look stale, with the reasoning, because an old saved password is the usual cause of a sign-in prompt that keeps coming back. A secret can be revealed one credential at a time, only when the tool is run as administrator, and each reveal writes one log line that names the target and never the secret.
readme.new_intro: Credential Viewer is a new tool in the suite, so everything about it is new.
new: The list never holds a secret: it reads the target, type, user and last-written time and shows dots.
A credential that looks out of date is listed with the reason, so you know which one to look at.
Reveal is one at a time.
A reveal needs elevation, is refused by name without it, shows one secret briefly and logs the target, never the secret.
A test searches the source to prove that neither path exists.
A stale credential can be removed after it is saved, so it can be restored.

plan.scope: The whole tool: build, engine, window, features, release
plan.goal: Credential Viewer ships as a complete, standalone C++ tool: it lists the credentials Windows has stored by target, type and user with every secret masked, judges which ones look stale with stated reasoning, reveals one secret at a time only when elevated and logs only the target, and proves by a search of the source that no reveal-all or export path exists.
plan.current_state: Nothing exists yet. This is a new tool, not a port: there is no AutoIt original and no `reference/au3/` folder. The repository holds the chosen identity under `brand/`, `DESIGN.md` with the Sidebar window, the kits, and the plan section it grew from under `docs/origin/resolute-D05-T06-s7.md` (that file also covers a display information tool and a connection viewer, which belong to other tools and are not taken). The engine's inputs are known from Windows: `CredEnumerateW` lists the credentials a process can see, `CredReadW` reads one, `CredFree` releases what either returned, and a credential carries a target name, a type (generic or domain password among others), a user name, a persistence setting and a last-written time. A process can read back the secret of a generic credential of its own user, but not the secret of a domain password. The tool runs unelevated; the reveal's elevation requirement is the tool's own rule and not a limit Windows imposes on reading one's own generic credentials. Windows' own list, `cmdkey /list`, shows targets, types and users without secrets and is the cross-check. Where Windows records which stored credential caused a prompt is not yet confirmed, so the stale judgment starts from what the credential itself carries. The SDK's framework, repair contract and chart control are planned in Resolute-SDK and not built.
inputs: `docs/origin/resolute-D05-T06-s7.md`: the plan section this tool grew from; only its credential items and its rule that a list showing every secret at once is a harvesting surface are taken.
`DESIGN.md`: the tool's identity and its window's sections, and `sdk/DESIGN.md`, the suite's contract.
`cmdkey /list`: Windows' own list of stored credentials, run by hand as the cross-check for what the tool lists.
outcome: `CredentialViewer.exe` lists every stored credential by target, type and user with each secret masked, and no row, log line or screen string ever holds a secret unless one reveal is on screen.

Credentials that look stale are listed with their reasoning; a reveal is refused by name when unelevated, reads exactly one credential, and writes one log line naming the target and not the secret; a stale credential can be removed after being saved and put back.
A test searches the source and proves that no reveal-all and no export path exists, and the Sidebar window of `DESIGN.md` works in light and dark at every scale, by keyboard alone.
plan.adjacency_rationale: The list is the Credentials screen, where a person finds a credential by its target, type or user. Reporting and audit are the Activity section, which holds every refresh, refusal, reveal and removal, each reveal as one line naming the target. Settings are the framework's pages. Permissions do not anchor on the tool as a whole, because it runs unelevated and listing needs no right the user lacks; the one gate is the elevation check at the reveal itself, in the engine. Reverse anchors on the removal of a stale credential: the credential is saved first, protected for the current user, and the undo writes it back.

engine.title: Credential Enumeration and Reveal
engine.intro: The tool's whole system effect, independent of any window: enumerating the stored credentials without copying any secret into the list, judging a credential stale with stated reasoning, and the one gated reveal. The tool runs unelevated; only the reveal needs elevation, checked at the reveal and before anything is read.
build: Put the credential store behind one interface in `src/core/CredentialStore.h` with a Windows implementation and a fake for tests. Done when: the engine's tests run against the fake and the Windows implementation is the only code that includes the credential management header.

Implement listing, the stale judgment and the reveal in `src/core/CredentialList.cpp`, `src/core/Stale.cpp` and `src/core/Reveal.cpp`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L credentials` passes against the fake store.
items: Define `CredentialRow` in `src/core/CredentialList.h` with target, type, user name, last-written time, persistence and secret length, and no field that holds secret bytes or text. Done when: a search of `src/core/CredentialList.h` finds no secret-bearing field and a test builds a row from a fake credential whose secret is the marker text `MARKER-SECRET`. Cheaper substitute: a row that keeps the secret and hides it in the view, which one screen change would expose.

Implement `ListCredentials()` in `src/core/CredentialList.cpp` over `CredEnumerateW`, copying only the row fields, overwriting the returned secret bytes with `SecureZeroMemory` and releasing the buffer with `CredFree`. Done when: a test with the fake store shows the blob zeroed before release and `MARKER-SECRET` in no row, log line or display string. Cheaper substitute: leaving the enumeration buffer unzeroed, which keeps every secret in memory until the allocator reuses it.

Classify each credential as generic, domain password or other with its type number, and carry its persistence (session, local machine or enterprise). Done when: a fixture with one of each type reports the right class and a `Session only` flag for the session one.

Implement `JudgeStale(rows, now, policy)` in `src/core/Stale.cpp` returning each stale credential with a sentence of reasoning built from evidence read: a last-written time older than the age in the settings, or a newer credential for the same target under another user name or type that supersedes it. Done when: a fixture with an old credential and a superseded one returns both with their reasons and a fresh credential with none. Cheaper substitute: flagging everything older than a fixed age with no reason, which states a conclusion without the reasoning.

Implement `Reveal(target, type)` in `src/core/Reveal.cpp` that checks elevation first and refuses by name, with a record in Activity, before any `CredReadW` call. Done when: an unelevated test against the fake store reports the refusal and the store's read counter is zero. Cheaper substitute: reading first and discarding on refusal, which already held the secret.

Make `Reveal` read exactly one credential and refuse a domain password with the reason that Windows lets no program read it back. Done when: a test asks for one target and sees one read, and a domain password request reads nothing and names the reason.

Write exactly one log line per reveal through the log interface in `src/core/RevealLog.h`, naming the target and never the secret. Done when: a driven reveal against the fake store leaves one line holding the target and a search of the log for `MARKER-SECRET` finds nothing. Cheaper substitute: logging the call's arguments and result, which writes the secret.

Return a revealed secret in a buffer type in `src/core/Secret.h` that zeroes itself when released and cannot be copied to a string or log. Done when: a test shows the buffer zeroed after release and a compile check shows no conversion to a log argument.

Cover every path in `tests/credentials_test.cpp` with the fake store. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L credentials` passes, and fails when `ListCredentials()` is changed to copy a secret.
engine.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L credentials` passes, including the unelevated refusal with zero reads, the domain password refusal and the one-line log, and fails when a secret is copied into a row.
engine.commit: core: list credentials without secrets, judge stale ones, gated single reveal

enhancements.title: Sign-in Problems Screen
enhancements.intro: The second section of the window: the credentials the engine judges stale, each with its reasoning, so a person knows which saved sign-in to look at first. It lists and explains; it changes nothing.

surface.fidelity: the Sign-in problems section, against `DESIGN.md` section 2.
surface.job: a person sees which stored credentials probably cause repeated sign-in prompts and why. Consumer: the list, read back against the engine's judgment.
surface.treatment: one row per stale credential with its target, user and the reasoning in a sentence, and an empty state saying nothing looks stale. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: a flag column on the Credentials list with no reasoning, which names a conclusion without its evidence.

build: Build the screen in `src/ui/SigninProblemsView.cpp` from the SDK's list control. Done when: the section shows the engine's stale rows with their reasons.
Cover it in `tests/signin_test.cpp`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L signin` passes.
items: Create `src/ui/SigninProblemsView.cpp` listing the results of `JudgeStale` with target, user and the reasoning sentence. Done when: a fixture with two stale credentials shows two rows with their reasons. Cheaper substitute: rows typed into the view, which show nothing real.
Show an empty state of one sentence when nothing looks stale. Done when: a fixture of fresh credentials shows it and it disappears when one goes stale.
Make selecting a row select the same credential in the Credentials section. Done when: choosing a row here and switching sections shows that credential selected there.
Cover it in `tests/signin_test.cpp` reading the rows through UI Automation. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L signin` passes, and fails when a row's reasoning is dropped.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L signin` passes: each stale credential shows with its reasoning and a fresh set shows the empty state.
enhancements.commit: ui: the Sign-in problems section with its reasoning

enhancements.title: Reveal One Secret
enhancements.intro: The one gated reveal in the window: one selected credential, only when elevated, shown briefly, logged by target, and never copied. It is the harvesting-surface rule made into a control: a person who needs one secret can have that one, and nobody can have them all.

surface.fidelity: the Reveal action and its result, against `DESIGN.md` section 2 and `sdk/DESIGN.md` section 11.
surface.job: a person sees one stored secret on explicit request. Consumer: the row, read back after the reveal ends.
surface.treatment: a confirmation naming the target, the secret shown only in that row for a short time then dots again, a refusal naming Reveal when unelevated. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: a Show passwords toggle on the list, which is a reveal-all with a friendlier label.

build: Wire Reveal in `src/ui/CredentialsView.cpp` to `Reveal(target, type)` for the one selected row. Done when: the secret appears in that row only and then returns to dots.
Cover it in `tests/reveal_ui_test.cpp` with the fake store and a forced elevation state. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L reveal` passes.
items: Enable Reveal in `src/ui/CredentialsView.cpp` only for exactly one selected row, with a tooltip saying why when it is disabled. Done when: no row and two rows both leave it disabled. Cheaper substitute: acting on the first of several selected rows, which hides the rule instead of stating it.
Ask for a confirmation naming the target before the reveal, through the framework's message surface. Done when: cancelling reads nothing and writes no log line. Cheaper substitute: a private dialog.

Show a refusal that names Reveal and says it needs administrator rights when the tool is not elevated. Done when: an unelevated driven run shows the message, reads nothing and leaves one Activity line.

Show the secret only in the selected row for a short time, then restore the dots and zero the buffer; the time is a framework setting with a default stated in `DESIGN.md`. Done when: a driven reveal shows the secret, then dots, and the buffer is zeroed. Cheaper substitute: hiding the text by colour, which leaves it readable to UI Automation.

Offer no copy of a revealed secret: no Copy command, and the secret is not exposed through UI Automation after it is hidden. Done when: Ctrl+C on the row puts no secret on the clipboard and a UI Automation walk after the hide finds none.
Cover it in `tests/reveal_ui_test.cpp`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L reveal` passes, and fails when the secret remains after the hide.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L reveal` passes: an unelevated reveal is refused by name with nothing read, an elevated one shows one secret briefly with one log line naming the target, and no copy path exists.
enhancements.commit: feature: reveal one secret, gated, logged and never copied

enhancements.title: Proof There Is No Reveal-All
enhancements.intro: A test, not a promise: a search of the source that fails the build if a second way to read a secret appears, or any function that lists secrets, writes them out or exports them. The credential list that shows every secret at once is the cheaper substitute this section exists to keep out.
build: Write `tests/no_reveal_all_test.cpp` that searches `src/` for secret-reading calls. Done when: it finds exactly one read call site, in `src/core/Reveal.cpp`.
Register it in `tests/CMakeLists.txt` under the label `proof`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L proof` runs it on every build.
items: Search `src/` for `CredReadW` and `CredReadA` and require exactly one call site, in `src/core/Reveal.cpp`, outside any loop over credentials. Done when: the test passes on the tree and fails on a copy of the tree with a second call added. Cheaper substitute: a code review comment, which does not run on the next commit.

Search `src/` for any function, command or menu item named for revealing all, exporting, saving or copying credentials and for file writes of a secret type. Done when: the test fails on a tree copy with a function named `ExportCredentials` and passes on the real tree.

Search the Windows implementation of the credential store for `CredEnumerateW` and require that every row-building path overwrites the returned secret bytes. Done when: the test fails on a tree copy where the `SecureZeroMemory` call is removed.
Run the proof as part of `scripts/check-all.ps1` so a release cannot skip it. Done when: `pwsh scripts/check-all.ps1` lists the proof gate and fails when the test fails.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L proof` passes on the tree and fails on each of the three tampered tree copies.
enhancements.commit: test: prove by search that no reveal-all or export path exists

enhancements.title: Remove a Stale Credential
enhancements.intro: A person who finds a stale credential can remove it, after it has been saved so it can be put back. Saving a secret to restore it reads that one secret, so it goes through the same single gated read as a reveal: elevated, one credential, one log line naming the target, and the saved record is protected for the current user and never shown or exported. A domain password cannot be read back by Windows, so it cannot be saved and is not removed by this tool. The record and the undo are the SDK repair contract's, which this section consumes once it exists.

surface.fidelity: the Remove action, its confirmation and Undo, against `DESIGN.md` section 2 and `sdk/DESIGN.md` section 11.
surface.job: a person removes a stale credential and can put it back. Consumer: the credential store, compared with the record.
surface.treatment: a confirmation naming the target and the reasoning, then the credential removed and Undo enabled. Cheaper substitute that fails the checkpoint: deleting without saving, which cannot be put back.

build: Save the credential through the repair contract in `src/core/Remove.cpp` before deleting it. Done when: a record protected for the current user exists on disk before the delete.
Wire Remove and Undo in `src/ui/SigninProblemsView.cpp`. Done when: remove then undo leaves the store as it was.
items: Save the credential's target, type, user name, persistence and secret through the repair contract's restore record, protected with the current user's data protection key, before any delete. Done when: a test finds the record on disk, and that it holds no secret in plain text, before the fake store's delete is called. Cheaper substitute: keeping it in memory or in a plain file, which is lost on close or readable by anyone.

Read the secret for the save only through `Reveal` in `src/core/Reveal.cpp`, elevated, one credential, one log line naming the target. Done when: an unelevated removal is refused by name with nothing read and the proof of `-L proof` still finds one read call site.
Refuse to remove a domain password, naming the reason that it cannot be saved and so cannot be put back. Done when: a test requests it and the store is unchanged.

Implement the delete over `CredDeleteW` for the saved credential only, after a confirmation naming the target and the reasoning. Done when: a fake-store test shows exactly the one credential removed and an Activity line written. Cheaper substitute: a bulk Remove all stale, which deletes credentials nobody looked at.

Implement Undo writing the record back with `CredWriteW`, disabled with a tooltip when there is nothing to undo. Done when: remove then undo leaves the fake store equal to before, asserted, and a first run shows Undo disabled.
Cover it in `tests/remove_test.cpp`. Done when: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L removal` passes, and fails when the record is not saved before the delete.
enhancements.checkpoint: `sdk\reskit\cmake\bin\ctest.exe --preset debug -L removal` passes: remove then undo leaves the store as it was, a domain password and an unelevated removal are refused by name, and the record is on disk before the delete.
enhancements.commit: feature: remove a stale credential after saving it, with undo

verification: A search of `src/` finds exactly one secret-reading call site and no reveal-all, export, copy or file-write path for a secret, as `tests/no_reveal_all_test.cpp` proves.

On a real machine the tool's list matches `cmdkey /list` by target, type and user, shows every secret as dots, refuses an unelevated reveal by name and, elevated, reveals one secret with one log line naming the target.
The window works in light and dark at every scale, by keyboard alone, and the release set runs from an empty folder.
